title: AWS CWI Training in Louisville, KY: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Louisville truck plant, power, bridge and distillery welding staff. Corporate, online or one-to-one. Quote on request.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Louisville, Kentucky: Six Days for Truck Plant, Power, Bridge and Distillery Welding Inspectors
html:
Louisville welds trucks, power plants, river bridges and the copper and steel that the bourbon business runs on. Each of those trades needs people who can read a weld map, check a joint against a code and put their name on the result. Atlantis NDT prepares Louisville welders, fitters, QC technicians and engineers for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination with a six-day (6-day) course that covers Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. You can take it three ways: corporate delivery at your employer's facility, online study at your own pace, or one-to-one sessions with the instructor. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification; Atlantis gets candidates ready and certifies nobody. There is no Atlantis classroom in Louisville. The company's offices are in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India, and every Louisville candidate is reached through one of the three formats. For a quote, send a Louisville CWI exam prep enquiry.

How do the six days work for a Louisville candidate?

The outline never changes: two days of fundamentals, one day rehearsing the practical, one day working inside the code book you will carry into Part C, one day of timed practice papers and a final day spent on weak areas and exam logistics. What changes is how the days reach you. The full day-by-day breakdown sits on the national AWS CWI exam prep page.

  • Corporate. A plant, fabricator or contractor in Jefferson County or across the river in southern Indiana books the six days for a group of its own people. Delivery happens at that employer's facility, with its fillet gauges, its weld samples and, where it fits, the code and procedures its crews already work to.
  • Online. An individual gets a study plan built on the six-day outline, course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, plus an instructor who answers questions as they come up. Nothing is scheduled. That suits someone rotating through shifts at a truck plant or working long weeks on a construction site.
  • One-to-one. One candidate works through the six days in one-to-one sessions with the instructor, either online or in person at a location agreed when the course is booked. It is the format for someone who wants to be pushed through the code book or who learns faster by talking problems out.

In every format the practice material is written by Atlantis to the topic areas AWS publishes. None of it comes from a real AWS examination, and AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course.

Where Louisville welds: the local economy, sector by sector

The truck and SUV plants

Ford runs two assembly plants in Louisville. Kentucky Truck Plant builds F-Series Super Duty pickups, the Ford Expedition and the Lincoln Navigator, and Ford calls it its largest and highest-revenue US manufacturing plant. In 2026 Ford announced a new paint shop there to replace the existing one. Louisville Assembly Plant is being converted to build vehicles on Ford's Universal Electric Vehicle Platform, starting with a midsize electric pickup that Ford expects to launch in 2027.

A candidate from a body shop should be clear about one thing: robotic resistance and arc welding on vehicle bodies is controlled by the automaker's own standards, not by any book offered for Part C. The CWI demand around the truck plants comes from what surrounds the line. New paint shops and plant conversions mean large steel buildings, platforms, conveyors and mechanical piping, all welded and inspected under construction codes. Tier suppliers that weld frames, brackets and fixtures often keep a CWI to run their weld quality program and answer customer audits. And tooling and equipment builders want someone who can judge a fillet properly before a part leaves the shop.

Power generation at Mill Creek

Louisville Gas and Electric and Kentucky Utilities broke ground in November 2024 on Mill Creek 5, a 640-megawatt natural gas combined-cycle unit at the Mill Creek Generating Station that the utilities expect in service in 2027. The project partners named GE Vernova, Vogt Power International (a Babcock Power subsidiary) and TIC, The Industrial Company, which also provides on-site construction oversight. A combined-cycle unit is a welding-intensive build: heat recovery steam generator tubes and headers, high-energy steam and feedwater piping, and the structural steel that holds it all up. That work is qualified under ASME Section IX and built to ASME's boiler and power piping rules, which is why a Louisville inspector heading for power work should look hard at the ASME option for Part C.

Bridges over the Ohio

No welding inspector in Louisville needs persuading that welded details on a bridge matter. In September 2011 the Sherman Minton Bridge, the double-decked twin tied arch that carries I-64 and US 150 between west Louisville and downtown New Albany, was closed after cracks were found in welded areas of a main load-bearing steel member. Crews attached about 1,200 short tons of reinforcing plate along both sides before the bridge reopened in February 2012. A later multi-year renewal of the bridge wrapped up in late 2024. Bridge steel for state highway owners is fabricated under AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, which treats fracture-critical members with extra care, and the people who check that work need to know the book well.

Distilling and process equipment

The bourbon trade has its own metalworking base. Vendome Copper and Brass Works, run by the Sherman family since 1904, builds copper pot stills in buildings on Franklin Street in Butchertown, and many large American distilleries use its equipment. Copper still making is specialist craft work that no CWI code book describes. The distillery expansions around it are another matter: new stillhouses and warehouses bring steam boilers, pressure piping, stainless process lines and structural platforms, and those are designed and inspected to ASME and AWS codes like any other plant.

Chemical plants and river terminals

West Louisville's Rubbertown chemical district and the terminals along the Ohio River keep maintenance welders and mechanical contractors busy year round. Repairs to process piping follow ASME B31.3, procedures and welders are qualified under Section IX, and planned outages bring short bursts of heavy welding where an inspector's job is mostly records, fit-up checks and visual acceptance before the NDT contractor arrives.

Who hires CWIs around Louisville, and what they ask for

  • Industrial general contractors and steel erectors working on plant expansions, paint shops and warehouses. They want a CWI who can run shop and field weld inspection to D1.1 and keep the paperwork straight for the owner.
  • Mechanical and power contractors on combined-cycle, boiler and process piping work. Section IX fluency is the first thing they test in an interview.
  • Structural and bridge fabricators supplying Kentucky and Indiana highway work, where D1.5 and the owner's inspection plan drive the job.
  • Owner quality groups at utilities, chemical plants and distilleries, who oversee contractors and audit vendor shops.
  • Testing and inspection firms that provide welding inspection to owners and building officials on larger projects.
  • Manufacturers and tier suppliers that need someone on staff to own weld quality and face customer auditors.

Across all of them the same three questions come up: which code are you strongest in, can you show verifiable welding experience, and can you write a report a customer will accept without rewriting it.

Which Part C code book suits Louisville work?

Part C is an open-book test on one code that you choose. Pick the book you will apply at work, because the score is only half the value; the other half is knowing that book cold on the job.

Your Louisville workCode book to considerWhy
Plant buildings, paint shops, warehouses, platforms and structural fabricationAWS D1.1Structural steel in buildings and industrial structures is welded and accepted under it
Ohio River crossings, interstate and state highway steelAWS D1.5The bridge code, with its tighter rules on main and fracture-critical members
Mill Creek, boiler and power piping, chemical plants, distillery steam and process systemsASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Procedure and welder qualification plus power and process piping examination and acceptance
Steel gas transmission and station workAPI 1104The pipeline welding standard that federal gas and liquid pipeline rules adopt
Aluminum structures and fabricationsAWS D1.2The aluminum counterpart to D1.1

Study the edition AWS lists for the examination rather than the copy on your shelf, since the two often differ. Background reading: AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5 and API 1104.

The AWS Louisville Section

Louisville has its own AWS section with a site on sections.aws.org. Its calendar mixes technical evenings with social ones: earlier meetings covered topics such as pulsed waveforms and cored filler metals, and recent events have included a disc golf outing and a section day at Churchill Downs. For a CWI candidate the section is worth joining for practical reasons. Working inspectors and QC managers attend, and they are the people who can confirm your welding history on the AWS application, tell you which contractors are staffing up and explain how local owners use the credential. AWS members also pay lower AWS examination fees under the AWS fee table, which AWS publishes on aws.org.

Where Louisville welders learn the trade

Jefferson Community and Technical College, part of the Kentucky Community and Technical College System, is one of the main local routes into welding. The KCTCS catalog lists a Welding Technology associate in applied science at Jefferson with shielded metal arc, gas metal arc and gas tungsten arc courses on fillet and groove welds, oxyfuel and cutting, blueprint reading, a welding certification course and a practicum, alongside a combination welder diploma and shorter certificates that include pipeline welder options. Union apprenticeships and employer training programs supply the rest of the region's pipe and structural welders.

School matters for the CWI because AWS lets education reduce the welding experience you need. Be careful about which row of the AWS table your schooling falls into. Completed trade or vocational courses sit in the four-year row; associate degrees in engineering technology, engineering or physical science sit in the two-year row. Whether a particular applied welding degree counts as one or the other is a decision AWS makes when it reviews your application, so ask before you plan around the shorter figure.

Booking the CWI exam from Louisville

Once AWS accepts your application, its confirmation letter gives you an eligibility code. You use that code to reserve the two computer-based parts, Fundamentals and Code Application, at a Prometric test center; AWS reports more than one hundred Prometric centers in the United States, and Prometric's own site will show the ones nearest Louisville. The practical is different. AWS runs Part B itself at its seminar and examination locations, so a Louisville candidate may need to travel for it. Check the current AWS seminar and exam schedule before you commit to a date, then book the Prometric parts inside the order and window your confirmation letter sets.

The numbers to plan around: 150 questions on Part A; hands-on tasks with AWS-supplied tools and specimens plus 46 questions on Part B; roughly 50 to 65 open-book questions on Part C; and a minimum of 72 percent on each part. AWS publishes its examination fees on aws.org. For a planning sheet that adds travel, the code book and time off, use the CWI exam budget planner.

Studying around plant shifts, outages and construction seasons

Louisville work runs on a few different clocks. Assembly plants run rotating shifts and heavy overtime when demand is high. Power and chemical plants schedule outages, often in spring and fall, when maintenance crews disappear into twelve-hour days for weeks. Construction crews lose winter days to weather and then work long summer weeks to catch up. The three formats are designed with that in mind.

  • On the online route, put the two fundamentals blocks in a quiet stretch, then carry your code book to work and look up the clauses that apply to the joints you see that week.
  • Practise Part B measurement on scrap coupons and cut-outs with real gauges; it takes repetition, not reading.
  • Hold the timed practice papers back for the two or three weeks before your Prometric appointment, when the scores will tell you where to spend the last days.
  • If an outage is coming, a one-to-one block booked before or after it keeps the code-book work from stalling.

Corporate: six days at a Louisville-area plant, yard or shop

A corporate course brings all six days to one employer's site for a group of its staff. In Louisville that might be a supplier near the truck plants preparing its quality team for customer audits, a mechanical contractor getting inspectors ready for a power project, or a structural fabricator that wants more than one CWI on its quality plan. The practical day uses the company's own fillet weld gauges, bridge cam gauges and undercut gauges on welds from its own floor, which makes the measurement practice honest. The code day can split between books if part of the group is heading for D1.1 and part for the ASME option. Timing can be planned around outages and production peaks. Each candidate still applies to AWS personally, meets the experience and vision rules personally and books their own examination; an employer cannot sponsor anyone around those rules.

One-to-one: online or in person

The one-to-one format gives a single candidate six days of sessions with the instructor. Sessions can run online, or in person at a location agreed when you book. It suits three kinds of Louisville candidate in particular: a supervisor who has to pass on a fixed date because a contract requires it, an engineer who knows the theory but has never had to find a provision in D1.5 or Section IX under time pressure, and someone who sat the examination before and needs targeted work on one part. Because the sessions follow the same outline, a one-to-one candidate covers the same ground as a corporate group, just at the pace that one person needs.

Eligibility and the vision record

AWS sets the welding experience it requires by education. A high school diploma means five years of welding-related work; a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology cuts that to one year; completed trade or vocational courses leave four. The experience has to be verifiable, so list each job with dates, the employer, the codes you worked to and someone who can confirm it. AWS also requires a visual acuity record on its own form: near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without glasses, plus a color perception test, performed by a qualified practitioner within the period AWS allows before your examination. Candidates short of the CWI experience can look at the Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI), which has lower thresholds. The full table is on the AWS CWI exam prep course page, and the CWI requirements and career guide goes deeper.

After the CWI: where Louisville inspectors go next

AWS keeps a CWI valid for nine years, with renewal applications due at the third and sixth years and recertification at nine. From there, Louisville inspectors tend to branch in a few directions.

  • Senior CWI. Inspectors who end up running a quality program for a contractor or utility look at the AWS Senior CWI; see the SCWI pathway.
  • Endorsements. AWS code endorsements widen the books you are recognized on, useful for someone who moves between plant buildings and bridge work.
  • NDT methods. Many inspectors want to perform ultrasonic or magnetic particle testing themselves. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies NDT personnel after training and documented method experience, and Atlantis provides that training: see NDT training in Louisville, VT Level 2, UT Level 2 and MT Level 2.
  • Compare credentials before you choose: the AWS CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II comparison sets them side by side. Atlantis offers API exam prep separately, as self-paced online courses.

For local inspection work, see ultrasonic testing in Louisville and magnetic particle testing in Louisville, and between study sessions try the Practical NDT welding workshop in a browser.

Nearby CWI pages and a Louisville quote

Candidates elsewhere in the Ohio Valley can read the CWI exam prep pages for Cincinnati, Columbus, Indianapolis, Nashville and St. Louis. For how candidates fare part by part, read CWI results by exam part.

To price the course, tell us whether it is for one person or a group, which format you want (corporate, online or one-to-one), each candidate's education and welding history in outline, and the Part C book each plans to choose. For corporate delivery, add the facility location, the gauges and sample welds on hand and any outage or production weeks to avoid. Request a Louisville CWI exam prep quote; the quote is given on request.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis CWI classroom in Louisville?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Louisville. You can take the six-day course online at your own pace, as one-to-one sessions with the instructor (online or in person at a location agreed when booking), or as a corporate course at your employer's facility. See the course outline.

faq.q: Who certifies me as a CWI if I prepare with Atlantis?
faq.a: AWS. The American Welding Society reviews your application, runs all three parts of the examination and issues the certification to those who pass. Atlantis prepares you and certifies no one, and AWS has not approved or endorsed the course.

faq.q: Which Part C code should I choose for work at Mill Creek or another power plant?
faq.a: The ASME option, which pairs Section IX welding qualification with the B31.1 power piping and B31.3 process piping codes. Combined-cycle and boiler work is qualified and built to those documents.

faq.q: I work on bridge steel for Kentucky or Indiana jobs. Is D1.5 the right book?
faq.a: Usually yes. AWS D1.5 is the Bridge Welding Code used for steel highway bridges, including the extra controls on fracture-critical members. See AWS D1.5. If your shop mainly does buildings and industrial structures, D1.1 may serve you better.

faq.q: Where do Louisville candidates take the CWI exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based and booked at a Prometric test center with the eligibility code from your AWS confirmation letter; Prometric's site lists the centers near Louisville. AWS runs Part B, the practical, at its own seminar and examination locations, so you may need to travel for it.

faq.q: Is the one-to-one option online or in person?
faq.a: Either. You get six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor, held online or in person at a location agreed when you book. The outline is the same as the corporate and online formats.

faq.q: Can a supplier near the Ford truck plants have the course run for its quality team?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format delivers all six days at your facility for a group of your staff, using your own gauges, weld samples and, where it fits, your code. Each person still applies to AWS individually. Ask for a quote.

faq.q: Does a welding degree from Jefferson Community and Technical College shorten the experience requirement?
faq.a: It can reduce it, but AWS decides by how much. Trade or vocational courses sit in the four-year experience row and associate degrees in engineering technology, engineering or physical science in the two-year row. Ask AWS how it will treat your specific degree before you rely on the shorter figure.

faq.q: Are the practice questions taken from real AWS exams?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes every practice question to the topic areas AWS publishes, and it never sees the live examination, so nothing in the course reproduces an AWS item.

faq.q: Can I add NDT training after the CWI?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training in VT, MT, PT and UT, and the employer certifies you under its written practice afterwards. See NDT training in Louisville.
